title: Music and Theatre Traditions

cards.b: The split between Hindustani and Carnatic music, the gharanas and the lineage of folk theatre are staples of Prelims. Mains asks for cultural synthesis.

The Natya Shastra and later Sangita Ratnakara (Sharngadeva, 13th century) are textual roots. Music divides into Hindustani (north) and Carnatic (south) after the 13th to 14th century, with Persian influence in the north. Key concepts: raga (melodic frame), tala (rhythm), swara (note), shruti (microtone).

• Dhrupad: old, solemn; Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior; Tansen at Akbar’s court; Swami Haridas.
  • Khayal: Amir Khusrau credited (disputed); Sultan Husain Sharqi; grew under Sadarang in Mohammad Shah’s time.
  • Thumri, Tappa, Dadra, Ghazal: light forms.
  • Gharanas: Gwalior, Agra, Kirana, Jaipur-Atrauli, Patiala, Rampur-Sahaswan.
Instruments: sitar, sarod, santoor, tabla, shehnai. Ravi Shankar, Ali Akbar Khan, Bismillah Khan, Bhimsen Joshi.

Foundation: Purandara Dasa (father of Carnatic music). The Trinity: Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, Shyama Shastri (18th century, Thanjavur). Forms: kriti, varnam, tillana, ragam-tanam-pallavi. Instruments: veena, mridangam, violin, ghatam, nadaswaram. M. S. Subbulakshmi (Bharat Ratna 1998), M. Balamuralikrishna. Melakarta system of 72 parent ragas (Venkatamakhin, 17th century; later reworked).

Folk: Baul (Bengal), Bhatiyali, Pandavani (Chhattisgarh), Lavani, Alha. Devotional: Rabindra Sangeet, Qawwali (Sufi; Amir Khusrau), Abhangs (Maharashtra), Sufi kalam. Modern: film music and fusion. Bands and the Vande Mataram and Jana Gana Mana traditions run through all of them.

Sanskrit drama: Bhasa, Kalidasa (Abhijnana Shakuntalam), Shudraka (Mrichchhakatika), Bhavabhuti, Vishakhadatta (Mudrarakshasa). Kutiyattam (Kerala), the only surviving Sanskrit theatre tradition, is a UNESCO Masterpiece (2001, listed ICH 2008). Performed by Chakyars and Nambiars.

• Folk: Ramlila, Raslila, Nautanki (UP), Jatra (Bengal), Tamasha (Maharashtra), Bhavai (Gujarat), Yakshagana, Therukoothu, Pandavani, Bhand Pather (Kashmir), Ankia Naat (Assam).
  • Modern: Parsi theatre; IPTA (1943); Habib Tanvir (Naya Theatre, Charandas Chor); Utpal Dutt; Girish Karnad; Vijay Tendulkar (Ghashiram Kotwal); National School of Drama (1959, Ebrahim Alkazi).

Many treat folk and classical as high-low. Others see them as a loop: classical forms draw on folk tunes, folk forms borrow classical technique. The gharana system faces a debate on whether it is a closed lineage or an open school. The impact of recording and film on oral tradition also divides historians.

Bismillah Khan, Ravi Shankar and Zakir Hussain made Indian music global. Tansen Samaroh (Gwalior), Sawai Gandharva festival and the Thyagaraja Aradhana keep tradition alive. Copyright in folk songs, GI claims and the Gurukul vs digital learning debate continue. Sangeet Natak Akademi and the Gandharva Mahavidyalaya preserve the arts.

  • Prelims tip: Trinity = Tyagaraja, Dikshitar, Shyama Shastri; Purandara Dasa = father of Carnatic; dhrupad = Man Singh Tomar; Kutiyattam = Kerala, UNESCO.
